name: Myles Lozano
headline: Mechanical and Aerospace engineering student, builder, and problem solver
major: Aerospace Engineering & Mechanical Engineering, Minor in Electrical Engineering
shortBio: Aerospace and mechanical engineering student with hands-on experience supporting military engine hardware and developing field-ready systems.
longBio:
I am a dual-major engineering student at Oklahoma State University pursuing B.S. degrees in Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering, with a minor in Electrical Engineering, graduating in May 2028.

In Summer 2026 I was a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at GE Aerospace - Strother, where I designed VGT inspection tooling and led a Stage 1 nozzle flow investigation for military and commercial propulsion hardware. Before that, I worked on engine remanufacturing at Springfield Remanufacturing Corp., and I currently develop client hardware at the OSU New Product Development Laboratory.

I also co-founded TriPoint Innovations, LLC, where I lead product development of Hunter Radar, an offline GPS/LoRa tracking device backed by a $75,000 USDA grant, and I lead engineering for OSU CEAT's 1st-place automated Homecoming display. I bring a strong work ethic, a rapid learning mindset, and eagerness to take on challenging technical problems.
